design: Independent tether-target-agents 0.4.0 distribution with exact asof-target-agents 0.3.11 compatibility dependency; optional Arrow 21 only.
Canonical branded parser/CLI/version without mutating legacy globals. Other core commands invoke the installed engine once; normal legacy outputs remain unchanged.
Demo/run exclusively reserve OUT; legacy execution occurs once in OUT/engine. Outer dossier changes only the exact first header; all remaining bytes match.
Manifest binds exact launcher code/version, original invocation hash, complete artifact paths/hashes/sizes and original engine receipt. Receipt binds manifest plus closed outer journal.
Outer verification checks roles, types, complete file/directory closure, current launcher proof, exact five-event dispatch/proof/terminal bindings and genuine current-originals core verification.
Outer --outputs-only is explicitly rejected; direct legacy outputs retain legacy verification modes.
External outer receipt SHA is optional but anchoring status is honest; independent retention is required against whole-tree replacement.

Failure and interruption retain outer failure metadata and available inner attempts; final receipt is published only after journal close. Published receipt bytes on a readback failure are quarantined.
Inspect tolerates a missing/empty failed journal and never redispatches. Engine130 is an interruption. Supervised subprocess interruption terminates/reaps once without retry.
meaningful_regressions: Real synthetic demo and copied synthetic run sources verified through genuine legacy admission.
Header and body substitutions rejected after manifest/journal/receipt rehashing.
Original source, engine receipt, launcher file, external receipt and role mutations rejected.
Boolean byte metadata and contradictory rechained launcher-proof event rejected.
Unlisted files and empty directories rejected.
Fresh/concurrent/existing output ownership enforced; concurrent test dispatches once.
Engine failure, interruption, constructor failure, journal-close/failure-append and final readback faults retain failures without a success receipt.
Branded help/version/errors, unchanged legacy parser, argument rewriting and inspect/verify no-redispatch behavior.
